title: Sum of Two Integers
prompt: Given two integers `a` and `b`, return their sum without using the `+` or `-` operators.
hints: Think about how addition works in binary: at each bit position you get a sum bit and a carry bit.
XOR gives you the sum of two bits ignoring carry; AND gives you where a carry is generated. A carry always gets shifted one position to the left.

Repeatedly compute carry = (a AND b) << 1 and a = a XOR b, then set b = carry, until there's no carry left. In Python, mask to 32 bits and handle the sign bit manually since Python integers don't wrap like fixed-width ints.

solution.approach: Simulate binary addition using bitwise operations. XOR of a and b gives the sum of each bit position ignoring any carry, while AND of a and b (shifted left by one) gives the carry generated at each position. Repeatedly apply carry = (a & b) << 1 and a = a ^ b, then b = carry, until the carry becomes zero. Because Python integers are arbitrary precision (no natural 32-bit overflow), mask intermediate values to 32 bits with a mask, and convert back from the unsigned 32-bit representation to a signed Python integer at the end if the sign bit is set.
